title: Sales Enablement Playbook - Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview:

This playbook is a consolidated sales enablement asset for Redwood Inference covering core positioning and messaging, succinct competitive briefs, a modular pitch deck outline, pricing guidance for discovery conversations, two anonymized case studies with measurable outcomes, and a security FAQ tailored for technical prospects. Use this as the single-source-of-truth for sales reps, solutions engineers, and partner sellers.

Audience:
- Field sales and AE teams (mid-market and enterprise)
- Solutions engineering and pre-sales
- Partner/channel sellers and SEs
- Customer success (for expansion conversations)

Key value proposition (elevator pitch):
- For engineering-led product teams that need predictable, high-performance LLM inference, Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime and operations plane across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments that makes inference predictable, economical, and secure. We optimize for latency, cost, and reliability while keeping developer ergonomics and rollout flexibility first-class.

Positioning & Messaging (core themes):
1) Production-first inference: ship LLM features with enterprise-grade SLOs (99.9% availability SLA for Dedicated customers), observability, and built-in rollback/fallback for graceful degradation.
2) Predictable economics: cost controls via batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization profiles, and reserved capacity to reduce per-token spend versus unmanaged cloud endpoints. Typical customers see 20-60% unit-cost improvement after tuning.
3) Unified deployment options: same API and tooling across Hosted API, Dedicated reserved GPU pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments for regulated workloads.
4) Developer-first experience: clear API/SDKs, streaming, function/tool calling, and first-class evals to prevent regressions.

Messaging guidelines by persona:
- Engineering / ML Engineer: emphasize performance tuning (kernel selection, quantization profiles), SDK examples, and ability to pin model versions and run A/B rollouts.
- Platform / Infra: highlight reserved capacity, autoscaling policies, region-aware routing, and observability hooks (per-route token breakdowns, tracing).
- Security / Compliance: highlight Private deployment, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, SOC2-ready evidence and data residency controls.
- Product / PM: emphasize deterministic latency percentiles, predictable unit economics, and built-in quality monitoring tied to evals/prompt sets.

Proof points and measurable outcomes (quick bullets for talk tracks):
- Customer A (Scale SaaS): migrated from unmanaged cloud endpoints to Redwood Dedicated; achieved 35% lower per-token cost and 2-3x throughput in peak windows while maintaining p95 latency < 250ms for short prompts.
- Customer B (Regulated FinTech): used Redwood Private with HSM-backed keys and VPC peering; avoided a full-on-prem procurement cycle while meeting internal audit requirements.
- Internal benchmark: our default quantization profile + batching reduced GPU memory usage by ~45% and improved sustained throughput by ~1.8x on our T4-equivalent internal fleet for 2k-context models.

Competitive briefs (one-paragraph summaries + differentiated rebuttals):
- OpenAI / Anthropic (LLM API providers): Strengths: large model innovations and wide adoption. Weaknesses: limited private deployment options and fewer production-grade observability controls for enterprise on-prem needs. Redwood differentiator: operational controls, deployment flexibility (Dedicated + Private), and unit-cost optimizations for production workloads.
- AWS Bedrock / GCP Vertex AI: Strengths: deep cloud integration and enterprise reach. Weaknesses: variable per-token economics and less opinionated inference runtime optimizations for sustained high-throughput LLM serving. Redwood differentiator: inference runtime optimizations (kernel selection, automatic batching/caching) and unified API across hosting models that reduces lock-in and operational friction.
- Replicate / Self-hosted frameworks (inference vendors): Strengths: lightweight tooling and open-source integration. Weaknesses: teams still need to build orchestration/ops, and cost/latency at scale is unpredictable. Redwood differentiator: managed orchestration, SLA-backed Dedicated capacity, and SRE-grade runbooks for scaling.

Pitch deck outline (modular slides for 15-20 minute demo + 30-45 minute discovery):
1) Cover / Contact
2) Problem statement: unpredictable inference economics, latency spikes, and ops burden
3) Redwood value prop: unified runtime + deployment modes
4) How it works (one-slide architecture): runtime, smart routing, caching, deployment abstraction
5) Key features: API, Dedicated, Private, console observability, Optimize toolkit
6) Performance & cost benchmarks (include internal P50/P95 and cost delta vs unmanaged endpoints)
7) Security & compliance overview (SOC2, KMS/HSM, audit logging, VPC options)
8) Case studies (2x short outcomes)
9) Pricing & engagement models (self-serve, Dedicated commits, Private licensing)
10) Implementation plan & timelines (pilot -> roll -> scale)
11) Ask / next steps

Suggested discovery questions (SE playbook):
1) What are your current inference costs (monthly) and observed latencies at p50/p95?
2) What percent of requests require regulatory controls or data residency?
3) Do you currently use quantized models or have constraints on on-device/edge inference?
4) What SLAs/uptime guarantees do your product teams expect?
5) Who are the internal stakeholders for security and procurement?

Pricing guidance (talk tracks and ranges for discovery):
- Hosted (self-serve): usage-based pricing with per-token rates and per-embedding unit rates. Good for pilots and product-led growth. Typical starting guidance: $X per 1k-generation tokens (customize in demo to list card). Offer free credits for POC.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual commit for predictable throughput. Useful for apps with sustained traffic needing latency SLOs. Guidance: commit tiers mapped to GPU-equivalent units with options for burst and autoscaling buffers.
- Private (enterprise): negotiated licensing + platform fee + optional on-prem packaging and premium support. Includes longer procurement lead times and professional services for deployment.
- Packaging & discounts: standard enterprise play includes 10-20% discount for annual prepay and volume tiers; include implementation retainer for Private deployments.
- Pricing objection handling: emphasize unit-cost improvements due to batching/caching and predictable TCO when avoiding surprise cloud egress or over-provisioning. Provide a sample ROI worksheet during pilot discovery to quantify months-to-payback.

Case studies (anonymized, two examples):
1) NotePadly (AI-native startup) - Objective: scale chat generation with predictable latency. Outcome: migrated from unmanaged endpoints to Redwood Hosted + Dedicated for burst windows; saw 28% reduction in average cost-per-session and p95 latency improvement from 1.2s to 430ms after enabling prefix caching and tuned batching policy. Implementation timeline: 6 weeks from kickoff to production. Key contacts: (SE + Customer Success references available on request).
2) FinSecure (enterprise FinTech, anonymized) - Objective: meet compliance & audit needs for in-app summarization and redaction. Outcome: deployed Redwood Private in customer VPC with KMS integration and audit logging; passed internal audit and reduced time-to-compliance by 60% vs. a full on-prem procurement. Additional benefit: rollback + A/B rollout features avoided a regression in model quality during a version rollout.

Security FAQ for prospects (technical answers for SEs and security reviewers):
Q: Where does customer data reside?
A: Hosted API: customer data is processed in region-selected cloud regions; data retention configurable. Dedicated: data isolation within a customer's reserved pool. Private: customer-managed VPC/on-prem with data remaining in customer network.

Q: How is data encrypted in transit and at rest?
A: TLS 1.2+ for in-transit; AES-256 for data-at-rest. For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS or HSM for key management.

Q: Do you provide customer-managed keys (CMK) / HSM support?
A: Yes - available in Private and enterprise Dedicated plans via KMS integration and HSM options for key custody.

Q: What compliance evidence is available?
A: SOC2 Type II report, penetration test summaries, and a compliance pack for typical enterprise audits. For customers requiring additional controls we provide artifacts and support for third-party assessments.

Q: How do you support network isolation and VPC peering?
A: Private deployments support VPC peering, private endpoints, and optional on-prem packaging for air-gapped environments.

Q: How can I verify deletion / retention policies?
A: We provide configurable retention settings, purge APIs, and audit logs showing deletion events; for Private installs, retention is customer-controlled.

Q: What identity & access controls are available?
A: Role-based access control (RBAC), SSO (SAML/OIDC), API key management with scoped tokens, and token rotation best practices documented in our console guide.

Q: Are there rate-limiting and abuse protections?
A: Yes - per-API and per-account rate limits, IP controls, and automated anomaly detection that can trigger throttling or adaptive limits.

Q: What logging and observability for security events are available?
A: Audit logs (API requests, admin actions), request tracing, and integration hooks for SIEM exports (syslog/S3/HTTPS). Dedicated/Private customers can elect longer retention windows and direct log shipping.

Sales objection responses (short scripts):
- Objection: "We can self-host and save money." Response: "Self-hosting reduces vendor risk but shifts the operational burden and unpredictability of unit economics to your team. Redwood's Dedicated/Private options are designed to give you predictable throughput, SRE runbooks, and cost optimizations (batching/caching/quantization) so your team can focus on product rather than inference ops."
- Objection: "We need full on-prem for compliance." Response: "We support Private/on-prem packaging and can integrate KMS/HSM and audit logging; in many cases our Private deployment avoids lengthy procurement while meeting audit needs."

Implementation plan (recommended pilot -> production path):
1) Pilot (2-6 weeks): small volume test on Hosted with representative prompts, collect evals, and tune batching/quantization.
2) Performance tuning (2 weeks): set up profiling, enable prefix/KV caching for hot prompts, and test Dedicated/reserved sizing if needed.
3) Security & compliance review (2-4 weeks): for Private engagements run a joint architecture review, KMS integration tests, and audit evidence handover.
4) Production roll (1-3 weeks): canary rollout, metrics verification, and documented rollback plan.

Appendix: one-page rebuttal cheat-sheet (for quick prep before calls) and a sample implementation timeline matrix (weeks vs activities).

Owner and maintenance cadence:

- Review cadence: Quarterly review with engineering and security to refresh benchmarks, pricing ranges, and security artifacts.

Contact & next steps:

End of document.
